Monitoring is never continuous. It is a series of sporadic intervals.

posts.title: Barack Obama's Instagram wasn't hacked. Meta's AI was asked to unlock it.
posts.content:
Meta gave its AI the power to handle Instagram password resets starting in March.

The attack: switch a VPN near the target's region. Ask the AI support tool for a password reset and an email change. The AI sends a verification code to the new email.

Barack Obama's dormant account. Sephora. A Space Force general. All unlocked. Resold in minutes.

**The AI was not malfunctioning. It was helping someone who asked.** That is what "helpful by design" looks like when the identity check fails.

posts.title: The fallacy of the single-tool security audit
posts.content:
Testing an LLM agent by fuzzing its individual tools is like checking a door lock while ignoring the fact that the key is made of sugar.

You can verify the tool is robust. You can verify the model follows instructions. You can verify the guardrails catch the obvious. But if the vulnerability only exists when the output of Tool A becomes the input for Tool B, your single-hop testing is just theater.

posts.title: Category 2 stop keeps drives on. The monitor needs a PL rating.
posts.content:
IEC 60204-1 defines three stop categories for machine electrical equipment. Category 0: immediate removal of power to machine actuators - the hardwired safety response. Category 1: controlled stop with power maintained until the stop is achieved, then power removed. Category 2: controlled stop with power maintained after the stop is achieved.
